messages:
alex: FYI SFO GPU pool is getting a bunch of preemptions/evictions right now, ~30% capacity down, several in-flight requests failing. detectors alerted 6m ago.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-1866004321. Pager routed to infra-sre.
infra-sre: Seeing provider spot reclaim events + autoscaler thrash. Nodes are rejoining but KV cache pressure causing OOMs on a few pods.
kevin: Are these preemptible G4s? any known maintenance?
maria: Provider shows maintenance + unexpected scale-in. This is not scheduled. Preemptions concentrated in sfo-1a.
kevin: Ok. Plan: shift non-reserved traffic to us-west2 and reduce new allocation to SFO until stable. Can we route by region tag?
eng-lead-sam: Yes — routing policy supports region preference + allowed fallbacks. Triggering a traffic shift will increase cross-region p95 but keeps customers online.
product-ops: Need a quick customer comm for status page + support triage template. Support wants ETA range.
support-lead-jen: Escalations: 3 customers with Dedicated reserved capacity already raised tickets. We should call them and offer options (failover, credits, or temporary dedicated burst).
maria: Short-term mitigations: 1) shift best-effort traffic to us-west2 (gradual) 2) enable model-fallback to quantized-cpu for inference groups with allow_cpu_fallback=true 3) drain evicted nodes to reduce noisy restarts.
infra-sre: Commands I'm running: 
```
# cordon+drain problem nodes
kubectl cordon node/sfo-gpu-03
kubectl drain node/sfo-gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# bump pool min size (temp)
terraform apply -var 'region=sfo' -target=module.gpu_pool -auto-approve
```
infra-sre: Also toggling autoscaler cool-down to 5m to avoid rapid churn.
kevin: How long to complete cross-region traffic shift?
infra-sre: Gradual shift of 30% -> 60% over 20-30m depending on backlog. Full normalization depends on provider reclaim cadence and capacity replenishment (~40-90m).
product-ops: Draft status page snippet for copy: 
"We are investigating increased evictions in our SFO GPU pool causing degraded capacity and higher error rates for some requests. We are routing best-effort traffic to us-west2 and enabling fallbacks for affected workloads. Impact: elevated latency and some failed inferences. ETA for capacity stabilization: 40-90 minutes. Updates every 15 minutes."
support-lead-jen: + please include contact link and note about reserved capacity customers — we'll call top 3 now.
devex-tina: Add quick config snippet for customers to opt-in to cpu fallback: 
```
redwood.route {
  region_preference = ["sfo","us-west2"]
  allow_cpu_fallback = true
}
```
maria: Cost note: cross-region failover will incur egress + spot premium. Estimated incremental cost for full shift ~ $7-12k/hr. If we want to avoid high egress, we can instead spin up temporary Dedicated nodes in us-west2 (higher baseline cost).
eng-lead-sam: For impacted high-SLA customers we should offer a one-time free dedicated burst while we recover — ops/legal approved?
product-ops: I can draft an offer template.
oncall-bot: Deploy bot: routing-policy update pushed to canary (svc-routing v2.1.7) by infra-automation at 1866004550.
alex: Confirming canary looks healthy — 5% traffic shifted, no errors yet. Proceeding to 30% next.
support-lead-jen: Called customer A & B. Customer A requested immediate failover -> we enabled their project flag to force region=us-west2. They reported degraded but functioning.
infra-sre: Node drain + pod restart completed on 3 nodes. Reclaim events continuing but less frequent.
kevin: Do we want to publish a tweet / public note or only status page?
product-ops: Status page + support portal only for now. No public tweet unless impact broadens.
maria: Proposed public status page update (short): 
"Investigating GPU evictions in SFO impacting some inference requests. Routing traffic to alternate region and enabling fallbacks. ETA 40–90 minutes."
product-ops: Published to status.redwood.ai at 1866004600.
support-lead-jen: Notifying sales for customers on trials.
eng-lead-sam: Heads-up: if evictions persist we'll need to shift more traffic which may push latency up another 100–200ms for some routes. Callout in comms?
product-ops: Added latency note in update.
alex: Pushing to 60% shift now. Monitoring error-rate and cost.
infra-sre: Error rate falling for impacted routes. Backfill capacity at 1866004660 shows +15 GPUs returning.
kevin: Any outstanding asks?
support-lead-jen: Keep escalation open for reserved customers and route priority support to me.
devex-tina: I'll prepare a short how-to for opting into cpu-fallback in docs repo.
alex: Thanks team. Next update in 15. Current ETA still 40-90m.
eng-lead-sam: :thumbsup:
alex: Update 1866004675 — traffic at 65% shifted, error-rate down 80%, continuing to monitor. Keeping incident open until normal capacity restored."
